notes: Agent 11's d0t check (OK'd by Agent 1): pass = TimerQueue busy <= ~3 % in threads.csv (window 3 d0: 62 %), no more > 100 ms frames than d0f, a clean close, no dump. Window: 5 s settle + 35 s warm-up asked, raised to 55 s by the 60 s first-frame floor (min_window_after_ff_s default, as in window 4), then 50 s measured; window 3's d0 had no floor (35 s warm-up). TimerQueue busy % is a per-thread share, so the longer warm-up does not change the pass rule. Functional only (hidden desktop): the frame numbers are not timing.
REX_TIMER_WAIT_BLOCKING must reach the game process: run-timing.ps1 sets it in its own environment around Start-Process and restores it after; run.json env_set shows it. Any value turns it on.

03:30 pair: -Only d0f,d0t when the file order was d0f, d0t. Re-check 03:53 (Agent 1): the order is fixed, so the file order d0t, d11t, d0f is the run order; run -Only d0t,d11t,d0f. d11t = window 3's d11 cvars (Agent 11's ON bundle R3) + REX_TIMER_WAIT_BLOCKING=1; its game.log must show 'Host timer resolution set to 1 ms (background opt-out on)'. Report per run: TimerQueue busy % (threads.csv), window fps, share of window frames in the 53-67 fps band (frame time 14.93-18.87 ms): python build/agent8/scratch/band.py <run dirs>. W4b runs d11t in place of d0t only if d11t holds fps within noise of d0f and cuts TimerQueue CPU (Agent 1).
